sections.h2: Selling land or a house in Burke County
sections.html:
Burke County runs along Georgia's eastern edge, across the river from South Carolina, and Waynesboro is the seat. At 827 square miles of land it is one of the biggest counties in the state, and it sits inside the Augusta metro area. Seven municipalities lie within it: Blythe, Girard, Keysville, Midville, Sardis, Vidette and Waynesboro.

Mid-2025 population was 24,408. The median home value is $151,600 and 70 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Sellers often hold farmland, timber or an older house in town, and in a county this large the parcel may sit a long way from the courthouse, so much of the paperwork below is easier done by phone or online.

Both offices share 524 Myrick Street in Waynesboro: the Board of Assessors in Suite B and the tax commissioner in Suite A. The assessors set values and send no bills. The commissioner collects for the county, the state and the Board of Education and has no say in values.

Mail for the commissioner goes to box 671 in Waynesboro, GA 30830, and the assessors use box 46 in the same town. Maps and records can be searched online through the county's assessor page and the tax commissioner's own website.

Appraisers from the assessor's office sometimes visit to update records. They wear a Burke County photo ID badge, drive a marked vehicle, measure the outside of buildings and photograph the exterior. If nobody is home they leave a door hanger or business card. To check on a visitor, call 706-554-2607.

sections.h2: How can a Burke County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the notice date to appeal. Assessment notices usually go out in July, so watch your mail then. The commissioner's site describes four routes.

  • Board of Equalization. The Board of Assessors looks at the appeal first and may change the value with a new notice. If it does, you get 30 more days to challenge that notice. If the value stays, the appeal moves to the Board of Equalization for a hearing.
  • Hearing officer. This is open only for non-homestead real property above $500,000, and a state-certified appraiser serves as the officer.
  • Arbitration. Say so in your filing, then submit a certified appraisal within 45 days of the board's acknowledgement, which it must send within 10 days. A hearing follows within 30 days of authorization.
  • Superior Court. Mail or file a written notice with the Board of Assessors within 30 days of the earlier ruling.

Arbitration costs depend on the outcome. The county pays if your value lands closest to the arbitrator's figure, and you pay if the board's value is closer.

Burke accepts applications year-round at the commissioner's office or the Board of Assessors, but to count for the current year the paper must be postmarked or received by the last day of the appeal period. The commissioner's FAQ gives April 1 as the cutoff for the billing year. On January 1 you must hold title, live in the house and claim it as your residence.

Codes you may see on the county's homestead page:

  • S1, the standard exemption: $2,000 off assessed value for state, county and school tax, with no age or income test.
  • S3 and S4, for owners 62 and 65 with income under $10,000, which add a $10,000 school exemption.
  • S5, SD, SS and SE, which cover disabled service members and the unremarried spouses of those who died in war.
  • SG, for the spouse of a peace officer or firefighter killed on duty.
  • L3 and L4, local school exemptions for owners 65 and older.

A refinance leaves an exemption in place unless the name on the deed changes. Vehicles you own must be registered in Burke County. The county commissioners, the Board of Education and the cities of Waynesboro, Sardis, Girard, Midville and Keysville have opted out of the statewide floating exemption.

The commissioner takes cash, checks, money orders and major cards, with a convenience fee on cards. You can also pay on the website or by phone at 1-844-898-2374 with your bill number.

A few answers from the commissioner's FAQ matter if you are selling:

  • Part payments are accepted, but interest and penalty keep running on the balance.
  • If the parcel faces a tax lien sale, phone the commissioner before sending any partial payment.
  • An appeal does not pause billing. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of market value and corrected after the final ruling.
  • A surviving spouse may petition for a year's support through an attorney or the probate court.

A mobile home that is not on homestead and was in the county on January 1 owes tax and must show a current decal. Unpaid taxes bring a 10 percent penalty plus interest, and a missing decal draws a fine of $100 to $300.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Burke County taxes?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels can go to tax sale, and the commissioner's website posts each sale date along with the list of parcels. Check that list for your parcel number if any year is behind.

Before you list, look up the parcel number on the commissioner's site and confirm that no earlier year is open. Returns are taken January 1 through April 1. Tangible personal property worth $7,500 or less in fair market value is exempt, though motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes are not. A buyer's attorney will check the real property bill and any personal property or mobile home account tied to the address.

Call the commissioner at 706-554-3223 and ask for a written payoff, then give it to the closing agent. Ask the agent how this year's bill will be shared between you and the buyer, because the county bills one owner and the split is a private agreement.

Confirm that your homestead exemption is yours alone: the buyer has to apply on their own once they hold title. If you farmed or cut timber on the land, bring any return or covenant papers you filed. A cash sale changes none of this, and the payoff letter is still the figure the closing agent needs. Keep the commissioner's phone line handy through closing, since the office is open weekdays and two Saturday mornings a month.

faqs.q: Where does a Burke County resident pay in person?
faqs.a: At the tax commissioner, 524 Myrick Street, Suite A, Waynesboro. The number is 706-554-3223. Weekdays run 8:30 to 5, and on the first and third Saturday the office opens 9 to noon.

faqs.q: How soon must a Burke County appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the notice date. If the Board of Assessors changes the value, a further 30 days applies to the amended notice.

faqs.q: Must I pay my Burke County tax bill during an appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of the property's market value, and the county corrects the bill after the final decision.

faqs.q: Is a part payment accepted in Burke County?
faqs.a: Yes, though interest and penalty keep running on the remainder. If the parcel faces a tax lien sale, call the commissioner first.

faqs.q: What does the Burke County standard homestead exemption cover?
faqs.a: The S1 exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value for state, county and school taxes, with no age or income test. You must live there on January 1 and apply by April 1.
